rationale: This is a leg-swap on the already-evaluated TwoCornerIntangibleAccountingSpread — the long corner is verbatim CashAndAccrualDoubleGatedIntangibleCapital and the short corner is verbatim UnprofitableAccrualSupportedIntangibleFirms — so the output is close to a mechanical linear combination of two archived signals with a largely predictable result, and any alpha gain will be hard to attribute to new economics rather than to double-counting the same oancf-based earnings-quality gate on both sides.

The Sloan-style balance-sheet reconstruction of operating cash flow is a legitimate, textbook fill rather than an arbitrary coverage patch and the coverage diagnostic (0.091 for oancf-based versus 0.121 for balance-sheet-only signals with the same xrd requirement) supports the binding-constraint claim, but this is a sample-extension robustness test of PreResearchCashGenerationIntangibleCapital rather than a new mechanism, and it risks a regime break because the reconstructed series omits non-dp non-cash items and applies mostly to the pre-1988 sample.

The motivating diagnosis is factually wrong — MIN of continuous RANK values produces no point mass or tied floor, so the claimed "large tied mass" explanation for the FMB/alpha sign conflict is unfounded — leaving this as a bare MIN-to-SUMRANK functional-form swap on an archived signal with no substantive economic revision.

A defensible best-of-legs consolidation whose outcome is genuinely uncertain (the internal-minus-acquired leg delivered strong alpha but weak FMB slopes in both prior forms, so whether goodwill netting survives the cash gate is informative), though the subtraction of two raw asset-scaled ratios inside a single RANK is crude and the incremental novelty over InternalNetAcquiredConjunctiveQuality is modest.

The stock-versus-flow distinction between the NWC/sales level and the annual accrual is a real economic distinction and the level version had the archive's best coverage, but NWC/sales is largely a business-model/industry classifier (it will systematically favor services, software and negative-working-capital retail models) and overlaps mechanically with the cash-generation gate, so an unconditional-industry robustness check is needed before crediting any result.

This is the most substantively motivated proposal in the batch: it identifies a genuine mechanical dependence in the leading specification (oancf appears with opposite sign in both gates, so part of the "complementarity" could be arithmetic rather than informational) and removes it by measuring the accrual from an independent accounting surface, with a clear falsifiable prediction and a plausible coverage benefit.
